title: NQMIX: Non-monotonic Value Function Factorization for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; architecture, off-policy actor/critic mechanism, SMAC comparison, three-run count, map-specific outcomes, ablation, and stated future-work limits checked
sections_checked: Title/abstract and method: unconstrained MLP mixer, actor and off-policy policy-gradient/critic target
Section 5: SMAC maps, difficulty, win-rate comparisons and three independent runs
Ablation: mixer modification across two combat maps
Conclusion/future work: additional maps and actor performance bottleneck
Appendix B: network/training setup
venue_year_verified: arXiv:2104.01939, first submitted 2021-04-05; no peer-reviewed venue identified in the paper/version reviewed
evidence_note: NQMIX reports higher win rates than QMIX and COMA on two complex heterogeneous-unit SMAC maps, but on a simpler map its result is between them. The main comparison averages three runs per method on three selected maps. The authors call for more maps and identify the actor as a possible bottleneck.

review_status: full-text audit complete; GVR theoretical optimal-consistency mechanism, matrix-game conditions, exploration threshold, predator-prey/SMAC evidence, five-seed setup, and stated limitations checked
sections_checked: Title/abstract and method overview: inferior target shaping (ITS) and superior experience replay (SER)
Sections 3–4: transition/self-transition nodes, sufficient conditions and exploration threshold
Section 5: matrix games, predator-prey and SMAC comparisons
Appendix H: failure cases under multiple superior actions and optimality/stability trade-off

venue_year_verified: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research volume 162 (2022); arXiv v1 submitted 2022-11-22
evidence_note: GVR's formal/empirical claims depend on exploration and sufficient conditions. The paper states the exploration threshold approaches one as agent count/action-space size increase and may be inapplicable to long episodes; SMAC experiments use five seeds, and the optional stability/optimality trade-off performs worse on some hard tasks.

title: Distributed Set-membership Filtering Frameworks For Multi-agent Systems With Absolute and Relative Measurements
review_status: full-text audit of the 12-page v1 complete; later arXiv v2 withdrawal and author correction notice separately verified. Preserve v1 claims as version-specific; do not treat the withdrawn marginal-framework derivation as currently validated
sections_checked: v1 title/abstract and related-work gap framing
Sections II–III: system model, uncertain-range derivation, neighborhood-joint and marginal-range algorithms
Section IV: projection/outer-bound performance theorem and proof
Sections V–VI: linear and nonlinear examples, five-agent simulation, conservatism and conclusion
Current arXiv record: v2 withdrawn 2025-05-24; PDF unavailable; author comment says equations 4–6 not fully correctly derived and foundational to marginal-based framework
venue_year_verified: arXiv:2305.15797v1, first submitted 2023-05-25; current v2 withdrawn 2025-05-24; no publication venue verified
evidence_note: The audited v1 proposes two distributed SMF frameworks and proves outer-bounding relations to a centralized filter's projected uncertain range; simulation examples cover linear and nonlinear settings. The later author withdrawal notice undermines confidence in the marginal-framework derivation; no independent proof audit of the disputed equations was performed, so claims are version-specific and not counted as validated positive evidence.

title: Beyond Monotonicity: Revisiting Factorization Principles in Multi-Agent Q-Learning
review_status: targeted primary-source 9-page full-text follow-up inspected; formal assumptions, continuous-time analysis, matrix-game/SMAC/Google Research Football benchmarks, five-run reporting, and single-state scope caveat checked
sections_checked: Abstract and Sections 1–3: contribution, single-state game, unique-optimum and regularity assumptions
Theorems 2–3: stability/instability results for approximately-greedy softmax-coupled gradient flow
Methodology: unconstrained mixing, SARSA-style TD(lambda), intrinsic-reward exploration
Experiments/discussion: matrix games, SMAC and Google Research Football; five-run win-rate plots
Conclusion: formal single-state scope caveat
venue_year_verified: Proceedings of the Fortieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI-26), 2026
evidence_note: The paper provides a later, distinct non-monotonic-factorization approach. Its formal analysis models a single-state game with a unique global optimum, smooth approximately-greedy behavior and regularity assumptions; empirical figures report five independent runs on SMAC/Google Research Football. This is contextual support, not a replication of NQMIX or GVR.
